Sure! Imagine you have a star that’s super massive—way bigger than our Sun. When this star runs out of fuel, it can collapse under its own gravity and squeeze into an incredibly small space. What’s left behind is called a **black hole**.

A black hole is so dense that its gravity becomes so strong that nothing can escape it—not even light! That’s why it’s called "black"—because no light can come out, making it invisible to the naked eye.

Think of it like a drain in a bathtub: once something gets too close, it gets pulled in and can’t come back. The edge of this pull is called the **event horizon**—the point of no return.
